sections.h2: Where is Rock Island County, and which offices touch your tax bill?
sections.html:
Rock Island County borders the Mississippi on Illinois's western edge. The seat is the city of Rock Island, and Moline, next door, is the biggest city. Jo Daviess County gave up the land for it in 1831, and it takes its name from the island now known as Arsenal Island. Total area is 451 square miles, 428 of them land, and the county is one of four in the Davenport-Moline-Rock Island metro area.

  • County Treasurer and Collector: mails the bills and receives payments at 1504 3rd Avenue, Rock Island, IL 61201.
  • Chief County Assessment Office: upstairs in that building, 309-558-3660. Staff are there weekdays through 4:30 p.m.
  • Township assessors: where questions about value start, across the county's 18 townships.
  • Board of Review: three people chosen by the County Board who rule on appeals.
  • County Clerk, Delinquent Tax Division: takes redemption payments, 309-558-3562.

sections.h2: How many homes and owners does Rock Island County have?
sections.html:
The July 2025 QuickFacts estimate is 141,869 people, a 1.9% decline since 2020, living among 66,873 housing units. Owners occupy 69.7% of homes, a bit above Peoria County's 67.0%. Half of owner-occupied homes were worth more than $150,400 over 2020-2024, rent runs $889 at the median and households typically take in $67,159.

Retail stands out for a county this size: 2022 sales reached $7,579,298 thousand, or $53,542 per resident. Transportation and warehousing add $720,001 thousand, and John Deere has its headquarters in Moline.

January averages a low near 13 degrees Fahrenheit at Rock Island and July a high near 85. Interstates 74, 80, 88 and 280 all run through the county. School districts named on the county's page include Moline-Coal Valley, Rock Island-Milan, East Moline, Silvis and Sherrard, and the commute averages 19.7 minutes.

sections.h2: When are Rock Island County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The yearly bill is cut into four payments here. According to the Treasurer, they go in order, each in full, with penalty interest added where it applies. Bills for 2025 taxes were due out on or before May 1, 2026, and the four dates were as follows.

Rock Island County installment dates for 2025 taxes, from the County Treasurer
InstallmentDue date in 2026
FirstWednesday, June 10
SecondMonday, August 10
ThirdThursday, September 10
FourthTuesday, November 10

All four have gone by. The pattern repeats next year, and the Treasurer posts the exact days once bills are out.

sections.h2: How can you pay Rock Island County property tax?
sections.html:
Six channels exist, each with its own cutoff, and a few close before the last due date.

  • Bank or credit union: through November 10, 2026 at participating branches. Bring the whole bill with stubs, and no cards.
  • Mail: address it to the Rock Island County Collector, PO Box 3277, Rock Island, IL 61204-3277, with a postmark no later than the due date.
  • In person: at the County Office Building. Cash, check, cashier's check and money order are taken, and cards and mobile wallets worked through November 13, 2026.
  • Drop box: in the alley and parking lot behind the County Office Building.
  • Online and phone: by e-check, card or wallet, with the phone line at 309-518-9200. The last day was November 13, 2026.
  • Autopay: online enrollment is offered.

The card processor, not the county, keeps the processing fees: $1.00 for an e-check, and 2.45% for cards and wallets or $2.00 when the transaction is under $82.00. Other charges are $30 for a returned payment and $2 for a duplicate bill. A mortgage company that wants a memo bill instead of stubs pays $5 per parcel.

sections.h2: How can a Rock Island County owner contest an assessment?
sections.html:
Township assessors set values as of January 1. The county assessment officer reviews and equalizes them, and the Board of Review takes complaints. If the result still seems wrong, the next stop is the State Property Tax Appeal Board, which the county's FAQ describes as a five-member panel.

Complaining that taxes are high will not win. The FAQ names three grounds: errors on the property record card, a market value above what similar homes sold for, or a fair value that still exceeds comparable properties. Useful evidence includes a recent appraisal, nearby sales, photographs of condition or a chart of comparable assessments.

The 2026 complaint session is over, and the county directs owners to the township assessor about 2027. Routine upkeep rarely raises an assessment, though a deck, porch, in-ground pool or fireplace can. The window is 30 days from newspaper publication, and once assessments are certified to the state the files are closed.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Rock Island County owners claim?
sections.html:
The county's Property Tax Relief page lists the programs, and the assessment office fields questions on each.

  • Owner-occupied: takes up to $6,000 off equalized assessed value if you lived in the home by the January 1 that begins the assessment year. File with the township assessor or at the county office.
  • Senior freeze: holds the taxable assessment steady while the rate keeps moving. Applicants need two straight Januarys of owning and living in the home, a 65th birthday within the assessment year, the senior homestead exemption and household income under the cap. Applications are due July 1 and renew each year.
  • Others: disabled persons, disabled veterans, returning veterans, natural disaster, and several charitable forms.

A state law signed in December 2025 lifts the senior freeze income cap. The county's table lists $65,000 for tax year 2025, $75,000 for 2026, $77,000 for 2027 and $79,000 for 2028, and it stays at $79,000 after that unless the General Assembly acts.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Rock Island County taxes?
sections.html:
Any installment still open after the fourth due date rolls into the annual tax sale. A certified-mail notice and newspaper listing follow within weeks, carrying a $10 fee. At the sale the county adds $94 in miscellaneous fees and $160 for canceling the sale and issuing certificates of redemption, and interest can range from 18% down to 0% depending on the winning bid.

Ownership does not move at the sale. The owner can redeem for two and a half to three years, with the buyer choosing the length. The County Clerk accepts cash, a cashier's check, a certified check or a money order, all in one lump. Call the Delinquent Tax Division, 309-558-3562, for a figure before you schedule a closing.

Escrow can hide problems. The county FAQ suggests checking that the lender paid each installment on the correct parcel, and not paying a second time. The county also runs an online lookup where you can pull a parcel's current and prior-year tax information, with years available back to 2003.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for Rock Island County tax?
faqs.a: Rock Island County Collector, PO Box 3277, Rock Island, IL 61204-3277, with the stub enclosed. A postmark on or before the due date is required, and the county suggests other methods given Postal Service delays.

faqs.q: Does Rock Island County take partial tax payments?
faqs.a: No. Partial installments are refused and installments are taken in order, with penalty interest included. Delinquent taxes likewise must be settled in one payment at the County Clerk.

faqs.q: When is the Rock Island County senior freeze deadline?
faqs.a: July 1. The application goes to the Chief County Assessment Office and has to be repeated annually. The county's income cap climbs from $65,000 for tax year 2025 to $79,000 for 2028.

faqs.q: How long can sold Rock Island County taxes be redeemed?
faqs.a: Two and a half to three years after the sale, as chosen by the tax buyer. Pay the County Clerk's Delinquent Tax Division, reachable at 309-558-3562, in cash, by cashier's check, by certified check or by money order.

faqs.q: What is the Rock Island County assessment office phone number?
faqs.a: Call the Chief County Assessment Office at 309-558-3660. It keeps weekday hours, 8 to 4:30, on the second floor of the County Office Building at 1504 Third Avenue in Rock Island.
